identity.title: Who will be the next to leave the Trump Cabinet?

scope: Factual post-window and historical-context collection; no interpretation, forecast, or probability.

facts.claim: Prior verified chronology: market created 2026-05-22 18:33:40Z; PBS/AP Gabbard resignation story published 17:40Z that day. The existing primary-window packet contains source hashes and receipt pointers.

White House notice dated 2026-06-11: Walter Clayton nominated to be DNI “vice Tulsi Gabbard.” This is a nomination notice, not a post-May-22 announcement of a departure by an already serving covered official; the frozen rule excludes nominees as departures.

CBS News report updated 2018-12-31 records four relevant past announcements: Sessions departure announced the day after the Nov. 6 midterms, at the President’s request; Kelly announced Dec. 8 to leave at year-end; Zinke announced earlier in December to leave at year-end; Mattis delivered his resignation letter Dec. 20, initially intending to remain until February, after which Trump advanced the departure. This is a contemporaneous outlet report, not an official records collection or representative frequency sample.

gaps: The bounded source check did not verify a later post-May-22 departure announcement, actual departure, Cabinet-wide reshuffle, or staying-on statement in the literal covered roles. This is a collection gap and must not be read as evidence of absence.
No direct official 2018 primary documents for Sessions, Kelly, Zinke, or Mattis were captured; the historical comparison rests on the CBS report only.
No press-secretary, Army, or ordinary ambassador developments are included as Cabinet evidence.
